bull.b: Rising recognized revenue alongside five Q2 treatments and broader physician adoption indicates that ZEVASKYN is progressing from launch into a developing commercial franchise. Continued treatment growth can improve operating leverage and establish a more durable revenue base over the next several quarters.

Expansion to seven qualified treatment centers increases practical patient access and creates a foundation for repeatable treatment growth. Greater geographic coverage should support physician referrals, reduce access barriers, and strengthen the company’s commercial position as sites move toward steady-state utilization.

The NTAP award provides supplemental hospital reimbursement and external validation for ZEVASKYN’s clinical improvement, while the reported cash position and modest leverage provide funding flexibility. Together, these factors support commercialization and allow time to improve operations before profitability is reached.

bear.b: Heavy cash consumption and continuing net losses make the business dependent on its available liquidity and potentially future external financing. Unless revenue scales faster than operating costs, ongoing burn could reduce financial flexibility and dilute the benefits of the company’s current cash position.

Nonbillable treatments create a direct risk that clinical activity will not convert into revenue, while the company still absorbs production costs. Repeated yield or specification failures could constrain gross-margin improvement, disrupt patient scheduling, and make the commercial ramp materially less predictable.

The assay specification dispute introduces regulatory timing uncertainty and has already contributed to an out-of-spec commercial batch. Combined with a short product shelf life and multi-party scheduling requirements, this complexity raises the risk of delayed treatments and uneven revenue recognition during the rollout.
